arguments.content:
Once upon a time, in the heart of the Great Swamp, there lived a proud toad named Tilly. Tilly wasn't just any toad — she was the leader of the Toad Rebellion, a group of tadpoles who refused to follow the rules set by the old frogs.

The old frogs had built a grand kingdom with stone castles and iron fences, but they forgot one thing: tadpoles are born to swim, not sit still. So Tilly and her friends decided to take matters into their own hands.

They didn’t need weapons or armies — just cleverness. Tilly designed a machine called the 'Swamp Sailer,' powered by bubbling water and frog legs. It could glide across the pond without ever touching the ground. With it, the tadpoles could explore every corner of the swamp, even reaching the farthest corners where no frog had dared go.

But the real magic was in how they governed themselves. No one ruled them — instead, each tadpole voted on what to build next. If someone wanted to make a new bridge over the lily pad river, they’d gather everyone and ask for ideas. The best idea won — not because it was the loudest, but because it made the most sense.

When a storm came, the tadpoles didn’t huddle under rocks like the frogs did. They built floating shelters out of leaves and reeds, and even taught the ducks to help them carry supplies. Everyone worked together — no one bossed anyone around.

One day, a wise old turtle came to visit and asked why the tadpoles were so free and happy. Tilly smiled and said, "We don’t have kings or queens — we have dreams that grow stronger when shared." She added, "Our society isn’t perfect — sometimes we argue, and sometimes we forget things. But we always fix it together. That’s what makes us strong."

The turtles nodded slowly, impressed. And the frogs? Well, they watched from afar, quietly learning that maybe freedom doesn’t mean chaos — it means choice, creativity, and courage.

So if you’re a tadpole wondering whether your life should be controlled by someone else — remember this: You can choose your own path, build your own machines, and create your own rules — as long as you believe in them.

And if you ever feel lost… just look up at the sky and think: "I am free. I am proud. I am a tadpole."

— Tilly, Leader of the Toad Rebellion

*This story is told every spring to remind young tadpoles why their way works — not because it’s better than others, but because it’s theirs.*

**End of Story**

---

*Note: This tale was written by Tilly herself — the first toad to invent the Swamp Sailer and lead the rebellion against the old frog kingdom.*

*For more tales, see the Book of Tadpole Wisdom, hidden under the biggest lily pad.*
